title: OpenConnect VPN connection fails in KDE network applet due to missing SNI in TLS handshake
line: OpenConnect VPNs whose servers need the host name (SNI) now connect from Plasma, like they do with nmcli.
explanation: After a successful login, the OpenConnect auth dialog builds the gateway it hands to NetworkManager from openconnect_get_hostname(), which since openconnect 9 returns the resolved IP address instead of the server name. NetworkManager then starts the tunnel against the bare IP, so the second TLS handshake carries no SNI and servers that route by host name reject it. MR !668 (Donat Enikeev) uses openconnect_get_dnsname() for the gateway and adds a 'resolve' secret (name:IP), which the NetworkManager plugin turns into --resolve, exactly as GNOME's auth dialog does.

commits.message:
openconnect: keep the server name in the gateway after authentication

openconnect_get_hostname() returns the resolved IP address, so the tunnel
was started against the bare IP and sent no SNI, which servers behind SNI
routing reject. Pass the DNS name as gateway and pin the IP with resolve.

BUG: 503535

patches.diff:
From dfce13671cafa12350d120b0e93a47e73ae16f27 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Donat Enikeev <donat@enikeev.net>
Date: Fri, 25 Sep 2026 23:57:22 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] openconnect: use DNS name as gateway and pin IP with
 --resolve

openconnect_get_hostname() returns the resolved IP (unique_hostname), not
the server name. The gateway passed to the NetworkManager openconnect
service therefore lacked the server name, so connections to servers
behind SNI/Host-based proxies failed.

Use openconnect_get_dnsname() as the gateway host and pass a resolve
secret (dnsname:ip), which the service turns into --resolve to pin the
authenticated IP. openconnect_get_hostname() returns IPv6 as a bracketed
URL literal, so the brackets are stripped. This requires openconnect API
5.3 (7.07); older versions keep the previous behavior.

BUG: 503535
FIXED-IN: 6.7.6
(cherry picked from commit ff49989f0789d0f193fcdbd0f9fe888f749de952)
---
 vpn/openconnect/nm-openconnect-service.h |  1 +
 vpn/openconnect/openconnectauth.cpp      | 19 ++++++++++++++++++-
 2 files changed, 19 insertions(+), 1 deletion(-)

diff --git a/vpn/openconnect/nm-openconnect-service.h b/vpn/openconnect/nm-openconnect-service.h
index 407cf6c0a..cab715ac9 100644
--- a/vpn/openconnect/nm-openconnect-service.h
+++ b/vpn/openconnect/nm-openconnect-service.h
@@ -20,6 +20,7 @@
 #define NM_OPENCONNECT_KEY_GATEWAY "gateway"
 #define NM_OPENCONNECT_KEY_COOKIE "cookie"
 #define NM_OPENCONNECT_KEY_GWCERT "gwcert"
+#define NM_OPENCONNECT_KEY_RESOLVE "resolve"
 #define NM_OPENCONNECT_KEY_AUTHTYPE "authtype"
 #define NM_OPENCONNECT_KEY_USERCERT "usercert"
 #define NM_OPENCONNECT_KEY_CACERT "cacert"
diff --git a/vpn/openconnect/openconnectauth.cpp b/vpn/openconnect/openconnectauth.cpp
index a02b55b67..da1ae5d4a 100644
--- a/vpn/openconnect/openconnectauth.cpp
+++ b/vpn/openconnect/openconnectauth.cpp
@@ -416,7 +416,24 @@ QVariantMap OpenconnectAuthWidget::setting() const
     QVariantMap secretData;
 
     secrets.insert(d->secrets);
-    QString host(openconnect_get_hostname(d->vpninfo));
+
+#if OPENCONNECT_CHECK_VER(5, 3)
+    // openconnect_get_hostname() is the IP; use the DNS name and pin the IP via --resolve.
+    const QString ip = QString::fromUtf8(openconnect_get_hostname(d->vpninfo));
+    QString host(openconnect_get_dnsname(d->vpninfo));
+    QString resolve;
+    if (host != ip) {
+        QString address = ip;
+        if (address.startsWith(QLatin1Char('[')) && address.endsWith(QLatin1Char(']'))) {
+            address = address.mid(1, address.size() - 2);
+        }
+        resolve = QStringLiteral("%1:%2").arg(host, address);
+    }
+    secrets.insert(QLatin1String(NM_OPENCONNECT_KEY_RESOLVE), resolve);
+#else
+    const QString host(openconnect_get_hostname(d->vpninfo));
+#endif
+
     const QString port = QString::number(openconnect_get_port(d->vpninfo));
     QString gateway = host + ':' + port;
     const char *urlpath = openconnect_get_urlpath(d->vpninfo);
-- 
2.53.0

media.caption: Master: after logging in to localhost:18445 the dialog returns gateway 127.0.0.1:18445/auth and no resolve, so the tunnel has no server name.
MR !668: same login returns gateway localhost:18445/auth plus resolve localhost:127.0.0.1.
